Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Holdings Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, please press star then the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Holdings's Q3 FY2024 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; David Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Elena Vargas, Chief Innovation Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. NutriFresh Holdings delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation across key categories, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, digital transformation, sales performance and channel strategy, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Consolidated net revenues reached $2.85 billion, up 8% year-over-year, or 6% on an organic basis excluding foreign exchange and acquisitions. This marks our ninth straight quarter of organic growth, outpacing the broader CPG industry average of around 3-4% as reported by NielsenIQ. Volume grew 2%, with pricing actions contributing 4 percentage points—a disciplined 5% average price increase across our core categories, reflecting sustained input cost inflation in commodities like cocoa, palm oil, and edible oils, which are up 15-20% year-to-date per Bloomberg data.

Breaking it down by key categories and brands, our Nutrition & Snacks division—home to power brands like NutriBar protein snacks and FreshCrunch chips—drove about 45% of total revenues at $1.28 billion, up 10% organically. We saw robust 4% volume growth here, fueled by our Health-on-the-Go platform launch, which includes low-sugar, high-protein variants that captured 1.2 share points in the $25 billion U.S. snack bar market per IRI data. Beverages, representing 35% of sales at $1.0 billion, grew 7% organically, led by a 12% surge in our functional water line SparkHydrate amid the premium hydration trend, similar to what we've seen from PepsiCo's Propel or Coca-Cola's BodyArmor. AquaPure, our flagship alkaline water brand, delivered 12% organic sales growth, gaining 110 basis points of market share in North America to 18.2% per IRI, driven by the Hydrate Hero campaign boosting velocity 8% through in-store merchandising and expanded e-commerce on Amazon and Instacart. ZestEnergy energy drinks grew 7%, with premium zero-sugar lines up 15%. Personal Care rounded out at 20%, or $570 million, flat organically as we lapped tough comps from last year's distribution gains with Walmart and Amazon, but margins improved meaningfully. GlowEssence skincare led with 11% growth, gaining 1.2 points of share in Europe to 14.5% via clean beauty formulations. Home Care, with EcoClean cleaners exploding 13% on biodegradable formulas, contributed steadily.

Gross profit expanded to $1.12 billion, or 39.4% of sales—up 180 basis points year-over-year. This outperformance to 46.8% in some metrics reflects multiple drivers, including 250 basis points from supply chain efficiencies like our SAP S/4HANA ERP rollout now live in 70% of plants, optimizing inventory turns to 8.2x from 7.5x, and $45 million in procurement savings through our global sourcing hub in Singapore, hedging 85% of 2025 cocoa needs 10% below spot. Pricing actions added about 300 basis points, with targeted 5-7% list increases on core SKUs like FreshWave sparkling waters and SnackJoy protein bars, maintaining elasticity around -2.5 and growing average unit revenue 6.2% ahead of 4.1% category inflation per IRI. Premiumization shifted mix favorably by 150 basis points, with higher-margin innovations like PureGlow collagen-infused skincare now 12% of personal care sales.

Diving deeper into gross margin factors—commodity costs, pricing, and mix—our basket faced 4% year-over-year pressure, with cocoa up 28% from El Niño-impacted West African harvests, palm oil up 12% despite sequential easing, and packaging up 3%. Proactive hedging covered 65-80% of cocoa at 15% below spot, saving $25 million, while RSPO-certified palm oil partnerships reduced exposure 15%. Net, commodities improved 90 basis points as a percent of sales. Pricing delivered +3.4% net after trade spend, with elasticity at -1.8, adding 120 basis points; we executed 6-8% list hikes on 70% of portfolio, like 7% on Crunchy Bites chips. Mix shifted +1.9 points from premium lines like Harvest Organics bars now 22% of portfolio, plus e-commerce at 50% margins versus 38% in grocery.

On pricing actions specifically, we implemented targeted 8.2% average list increases, down from Q2's 11.5%, using AI revenue management to segment by elasticity—4-6% on high-elasticity essentials like ValuePack detergents, 12-15% on premiums like organic kombucha akin to PepsiCo's Bubly. Trade spend depth fell 10%, shifting to loyalty via GCB Rewards with 25 million users. This drove 6.8% constant currency revenue growth: +8.2% pricing offset -1.4% volume, with elasticity -0.65 better than modeled. North America pricing 7.9% with flat volumes, Europe 9.1% but -2.8% volumes, emerging +1.2% volumes.

Geographically, we derive 58% from developed markets like North America and Western Europe, 42% emerging including Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and Middle East & Africa. Total revenues grew 7.2% reported to around our scale, 8.7% ex-FX, 6.4% organic. Developed markets +2.8% organic, resilient amid pressures: North America (35% total) +3.5% on 4.2% price/mix offsetting -0.7% volume, VitalPure hydration gaining 1.2 points to 28% ACV, CrunchElite bars outperforming by 500 bps. Europe +1.1%, pressured by UK/Germany sentiment, but GlowEssence skincare +5% via DTC now 18% of sales. Emerging markets +12.6% organic, 70% of uplift: APAC 18.4% led by China 20% on ZenBrew teas, India 25% on FreshBurst sachets; Latin America 9.8% with Brazil +11% on TropiCrunch; MENA +14% on NutriBoost. E-commerce 25% in emerging vs. 15% developed.

Competitively, the landscape is intense with CPG market +2.1% but branded volumes -1.8%. Peers like P&G and Unilever eroded 20-40 bps share; PepsiCo deepened beverage discounts 15-20%, dipping margins to 32.4%; Reckitt flooded Lysol BOGOs pressuring our air care; private labels like Walmart Great Value +8.7%, eroding 0.9 points. We optimized promos with AI elasticity modeling, cutting ineffective spend 18%, velocity steady at 22.3 units/store week. Countered PepsiCo with VitaQuench premium RTDs gaining 450 bps convenience distribution; in yogurt, CleanLabel probiotics +4.2% share to 11.8%; Europe Zero Waste trail mix for 15% share recovery. Emerging: localized pimenta toothpaste reversed Colgate losses. Pillars: premiumization (35% pipeline +20% tiers like NeuroBoost bars), agility (12 divestitures, $180M recycled), data-led CPG Nexus (27% stockout cut), sustainability (92% Scope 3 audited, 78/100 Sustainalytics).

Strategically, our Accelerate 2025 playbook—Thrive 2025 pillars—shows progress: portfolio pruning divested legacy brands for $150-180M, recycling to innovation (12 NPDs, VitalGlow 25% penetration); digital with AI demand sensing to 92-93% accuracy, e-com 18-22% sales, NovaDirect 42% repeat; sustainability 45-95% recyclable packaging, Scope 3 -15%, regenerative ag 40% cocoa/palm, AA MSCI; resilience localized 65% NA production, AI forecasting -22% stockouts. These drove 7% organic, 180 bps margin expansion.

Cash flow robust $550M quarter, $1.3B YTD, $300M capex on automation like Ohio robotics -15% labor. Net debt/EBITDA 2.1x, $1.2B liquidity, $250M repurchases toward $1.5B authorization. Adjusted operating income $420M, +12%, margin 14.7% +110 bps. Diluted adjusted EPS $0.92, +15%, beating guidance.

Outlook: Q4 organic 5-6%, op margin +50-75 bps, EPS $0.95-$0.98. FY2024 raised: organic +6-7%, op margin 14.6-14.8%, EPS $3.72-$3.76 (+14%). FY2025 organic 5-7%, margin 15.2-15.5% via $200M productivity, EPS +10-12%, assuming moderating inflation, stable FX. Q4 gross margins 47.0-47.5%, long-term 48%+ via Factory 4.0, vertical integration, e-com shift.

NutriFresh is positioned to outperform as consumers premiumize health/convenience like peers P&G, Colgate.

Next, Lisa Patel will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We're seeing strong engagement across all channels, especially with our new Health-on-the-Go campaign, which has driven trial rates up 22% for NutriBar and SparkHydrate via targeted TikTok and Instacart integrations. We've optimized promotional cadences, reducing depth 10% while lifting ROAS to 5.5x on Gen Z-focused efforts for ZestEnergy. Sustainability messaging around 100% rPET bottles and clean-label probiotics has boosted repeat purchases 18%, aligning with consumer priorities in eco and health.

Following me, David Kim will discuss supply chain performance.

David Kim:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. Our Procure-to-Pay 2.0 and Precision Sourcing programs, with AI hedging and blockchain traceability, mitigated cocoa/palm volatility, delivering 90 bps savings. SAP rollout and IoT predictive maintenance across 70% of plants hit 8.2x turns; new Juarez and Vietnam hubs cut lead times 30%, localized 65% NA production. Carbon footprint down via RSPO 95% palm, regenerative partners, targeting net-zero Scope 3 by 2035. AI demand sensing with Blackbook improved forecast 92%, stockouts -30%.

After me, Elena Vargas will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Elena Vargas:
Thank you, David. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent launches like VitalGlow plant-based snacks and NeuroBoost nootropic bars have been well-received, achieving 25% household penetration in test markets within 90 days and projected $450M FY25 revenue. CleanLabel yogurts with A2 protein gained 4.2% share; Zero Waste trail mix and microbiome actives in oral care position us for premium tiers. R&D hubs in Singapore and Shanghai focus on functional hydration and precision fermentation, matching Mondelez/Kellogg velocity with 35% health-wellness revenue.

Finally, Raj Singh will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Elena. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving sales execution. E-commerce now 18-22% of sales, up from 12-15%, with 25% penetration in emerging via Shopee/Mercado Libre, AR try-ons boosting beauty conversion 40%. Retail partnerships like Costco multi-packs and Target preferred status drove 92% ACV; omnichannel velocity 1.8x category, clubs +9% comps. Emerging acceleration added ASEAN/Vietnam hubs; North America fortress with Walmart/Amazon gains.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions... Our first question comes from John Doe with Firm A.

John Doe:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Elena Vargas:
Great question, John. Sustainability is core to our Thrive 2025 strategy. We've hit 95% recycled content in PET for beverages like SparkHydrate, reducing virgin plastic 28% and saving $80M; 45% packaging recyclable overall, aligning with EU PPWR and earning Target preference. Scope 3 down 15% via regenerative cocoa/palm with 500+ Brazilian farmers, blockchain via IBM Food Trust 100% high-risk ingredients. EcoClean biodegradable cleaners and refillables now 40% personal care gained 130 bps share to 16.8%, lifting loyalty 18%—consumers prioritize ESG, 45% U.S. households per McKinsey, and our 78/100 Sustainalytics score enables 5% pricing power.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Firm B.

Jane Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Jane. Emerging markets are our high-growth engine at 42% revenues, +12.6% organic Q3. We're targeting 60/40 developed/emerging by FY26 via $1.2B capex 65% on builds like Vietnam ASEAN hub mirroring Nestlé. APAC 18.4% led by India 25% FreshBurst via Shakti networks 2.5M outlets, China 20% ZenBrew RTD teas 15% share; LatAm 9.8% Brazil TropiCrunch +2.5 pts vs. Mondelēz, Mexico nearshoring. Digital GTM with Flipkart/Shopee 25% e-com, localized halal/small SKUs. Q4 emerging 13-15% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Firm C.

Mike Johnson:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

Michael Chen:
Sure, Mike. Inflation persists—cocoa/palm +15-28%—but we've disciplined: Q3 8.2% list prices phased by region/channel, AI analytics segmenting elasticity -0.65 portfolio. High-elasticity 4-6%, premiums 12-15%; net +3.4-8.2% drove revenue despite -1.4% volume stabilization from Q2's -2.1%. Demand resilient in premium health (volumes +2.1% beverages), countered private label with EDLP hero SKUs. NA flat volumes, emerging +1.2%; Q4 5-7% pricing as commodities ease (corn -15%). Protected margins +210 bps to 42.3-46.8%, premium mix 28-42%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Firm D.

Emily Chen:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

David Kim:
Excellent point, Emily. AI is transformative: Blackbook demand sensing 92-93% accuracy, -30% stockouts/-22%; NielsenIQ partnership optimizes promos 18% spend cut. IBM Watson procurement shaved 8% logistics; dynamic pricing simulates 10k scenarios; CPG Nexus integrates POS/social/satellite for 27% stockout reduction, 15% facings boost. Factory 4.0 IoT predictive maintenance 12 plants, 2-3% COGS cut like Unilever; Palantir-like forecasting mitigated Red Sea/El Niño to 50 bps vs. peers' 200 bps.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders, executing our Accelerate 2025 playbook to outpace the industry at 5-7% amid trading-down dynamics. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NutriFresh Holdings Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
